pulls.title: supoort IRR data in rdap
pulls.author: maggarwal13
pulls.body:
The core specifications for RDAP defines core object types, but it does
not contain objects for Internet Routing Registries (IRRs). This document is
intended to address this gap.

comments.body:
Ideally "members" can be expanded to IP or routeSet Object class but members attributes also supports  below syntax 

"members: 5.0.0.0/8^+, 30.0.0.0/8^24-32, rs-foo^+" which will be difficult to expand.

May be we can put RIR search object for such cases. What do you  guys think? Should we keep it as list of strings for simplicity ?
"members" here can easily be expanded to autnum and asSet object class, but for consistency with routeSet I decided to go with  array of strings

For this change I took a hint from Andy's work [route-policy](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-newton-weirds-route-policy-00) But there he mentions order of objects needs to be preserved but as per my understanding of rfc2280#section-6.1 ordering might not be necessary.

reviews.author: anewton1998
reviews.body:
Good start.

I left comments about using the extension Id and link relationships that would apply to most of the object classes.

comments.body: Extension is the common term used instead of support.

if you change it to "extension" be sure to change this as well.

BTW, no need to change the repo name.
regext
regext@ietf.org
ICANN
I would shorten the extension id to "irr" or "irr0". The RDAP part is given, and RDAP extensions that include opaque major versioning tend to start with 0 instead of 1 (that's not a rule though).
Each of these needs to be prefixed with the extension id, such as "irrRdap1_route". See my comment about using "irr0".
object class names also need to be prefixed with the extension Id: "irr0_route".

Expanding on this could be useful. A link to an RDAP autnum object and network object would be good. And for this reason, we should think about defining relationships, such as "rdap_irr0_autnum" and "rdap_irr0_ipNetwork". Thoughts?

I agree, we have rdapConformances like rirSearch1 , autnums etc...
I can change it to irr0 to be consistent

Well we do not prefix extension_id for any other path segments, so to be consistent may be we should not ?  I remember a discussion about  an extension RFC , are you suggesting this change w.r.t to that ?

It might help the cause to have a stronger rationale about why having the IRR registered data in RDAP would be useful. Is it because the registries are in general moving away from Whois to RDAP? Or, is there a more specific value-add?
"protocol" -> "specification" ... something the IESG flagged for more recent RDAP extensions.

In addition to prefixing new JSON members and object class names with the extension id, the new path segments should also be prefixed (per the RDAP Extensions draft). E.g., "route" -> "irr0_route".

Also, good to URL-encode reserved characters like ":" in the examples for the new path segments.
Should there be a "/" between the route and origin portions of this lookup path segment? That could help with parsing (particularly the CIDR length) in case needed on the client side.
To help map better to the RPSL, should "prefix" not be called "route"? IMO, good to do so for RPSL-related JSON members, for ease of comprehension.

At the risk of bloating the response with such objects, would it not be better to align it with the RPSL and have instead just an array of CIDR strings here? Since one could later easily use these "natural" CIDR identifiers to look up IP network objects.
Please see above comment.

Would be good to point to the section from RFC 2622 for this field. Similarly, for other fields where we say "as specified by RPSL". Since this is intended as a standards-track specification, more precise references should help the implementors.

This is a more general comment: Should we have a member for the raw RPSL in each of the new IRR object classes? That could help in case the current data structure does not suffice in capturing all the RPSL for this object. It should also help from the WYSIWYG and "what's actually in the field" angles, I think. :)

Knowing some RIRs do not support the peering-set and filter-set RPSL functionality, wonder if these RPSL classes should be optional for this new extension? In other words, what RPSL classes are required to be implemented in RDAP, versus not.

The expired draft had a similar discussion point: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-newton-weirds-route-policy-00#auto-8
Is there a reason for referring obsolete RFC 2280?
Curious how this would interplay with the RDAP Geofeed extension (RFC 9877)? :)

To add to Andy's comment about registering new link relations, wonder if we should also leverage "item" and "collection" link relations that are mentioned in the expired draft (https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-newton-weirds-route-policy-00)?
Should it not be a AS number instead, given the related ASN object might not have been registered with the registry?
Beside lookup queries, are there any useful search and/or reverse search queries we should be defining in this specification?
A good idea. If we do rename it to route should it be a string in CIDR notation only rather than IP object ?
Yes , I agree. I will also look at other attributes where we can make the similar change
Thanks for pointing this out. I will change at other places too.
Yes. We should then try matching types from the RPSL.
I agree, I will make change as per RDAP Extensions draft. Also I will use documentation prefix example instead . Good point to URL encode it. I will make these changes.
route object primary key consists of both a prefix and ASN together. I prefer to keep both in single path segment and URL encode the key.
On a second thought, route consists of both prefix and ASN . So it's misleading to have route just as prefix.

It should not be necessary if we can define all attributes  values as either reference to another object or RAW string. It should be possible to recreate the raw RPSL from the RDAP response. We should perform  a cross RIR survey for IRR data to make sure the data structure captures all RPSL for this object
Completely Agree, We should document such object types as Optional. I will review IRR data from other IRR and change the object type to optional wherever it's needed.
By mistake, I will correct it accordingly :)
I will remove country attribute from route. It is not required
Also country is seperate from Geofeed in Resource object types. We support both
Yes, I will keep this point open and first focus on finalising the data structure.

IMO, good to stick with RPSL terms and semantics when mapping to RDAP object classes. Otherwise, we might end up with a confusing taxonomy vis-a-vis RPSL. One exception to that would be maintainers where mapping them to RDAP entities should help with richer search, I think.

AIU, sometime the RPSL is quite involved to be captured by structured fields. Also, structured data from a directory services perspective is generally something that one needs to make things searchable. That helps determine what data to structure versus not. IMO, raw RPSL would become the catch-all in case the structured data falls short in capturing the full semantics of the RPSL for a particular class. We could re-visit this later.
Yes, good to match RPSL types, especially given range operators and regular expressions.

Not sure; since like a CIDR address string for "route", an ASN string for "origin" (irrespective of whether registered or not) would simply act as a natural identifier if it could be looked up. Perhaps good to start with data structures that capture RPSL types and then determine where expanding them to contained RDAP objects makes sense. Otherwise, there is a risk of bloating responses inadvertently.
Since RFC 2622 doesn't seem to contain this field for the "route" class, agree good to remove it, for now.
Good idea. Both CIDR address and ASN strings are considered natural identifiers for RDAP lookups.
OK.
Good idea.
Agreed.

On further thought, IMO, it'd be better to have separate path segments for the CIDR address (route) and ASN (origin) parts of a route lookup query by introducing a "/" between them, as in `irr0_route/<IP prefix of the interAS route>/<AS that originates the route>`. Since most registries would more likely be storing the route and the origin as 2 separate fields in the database, together forming a compound primary key, not having the server figure out where the CIDR address part ends and the ASN part begins in absence of that delimiting "/" would greatly help with query processing. It should be easier to cull query values from, say, `irr0_route/10.0.0.0/16/65536` than `irr0_route/10.0.0.0/1665536`, no?
Decided to keep it as array of strings see previous comment for route "members" attribute discussion
Agree to prefix the extension_id as per other discussions
Done, changed to irr0
Yes you are right , for autnum search we do not prefix "AS" so  without "/" it will not work. I will change to add path segment
"irr0_route" instead.
Typically, in RDAP specs, "handle" is defined as "a string representing a registry-unique identifier of the object-in-question". That way it could be a UUID instead, if so designed.
Ok, I will change it to CIDR address

For route object unique identifier is combination of prefix and origin n RPSL. 
for example: 192.0.2.0/24AS65538

But since we do not suffix "AS" in origin so should be we have handle as  "1192.0.2.0/24/65538" which will mirror the lookup path segment for route.

Should autnumSet also not prefix AS similar to autnum lookup's? 

Should this be changed to :
https://example.com/rdap/irr0_autnumSet/01121978 instead?
Added text "Support for peering-set, rtr-set and filter-set is optional and may be provided at the discretion of the implementation."
I have corrected tis at few more places. Thanks for pointing this out
After discussing with Ed too, I have  renamed "prefix" to "route" to match with RPSL

My key point is that the spec should not pre-define the structure of the "handle" field to allow registries the leeway for how they would like to unique-ify records, say, using a UUID or a sequence. Every object class in RFC 9083 defines "handle" as "a registry-unique identifier" and leaves it at that. Furthermore, one can always define multiple lookup endpoints, say, one by handle and another by the route-origin combo (natural identifier). For a similar, please see: https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-regext-rdap-rpki-02.html#name-lookup-2.
This is great. Such section references make the spec more precise. :)
Thanks for explaining. Makes sense to leave it to RIR.
Thanks for suggesting this

Since we are not expanding the objects to avoid risk of bloating the response , I think it's good idea. 
But some attributes might exists in other RIR (although redirect will work ) and some might not expand properly. 
For ex:  members:  0.0.0.0/0^1-5 . Although with RIR search it could be possible to expand now but will make server implementation difficult as server need to parse them properly. What do you suggest ?  Although I still need to give a thought around Andy's comment about  "rdap_irr0_autnum" and "rdap_irr0_ipNetwork"
Would it be a better example with a CIDR string instead? Say, "192.0.2.0/24" or similar.
"registry unique" -> "registry-unique"?
A whole example would be good.
